title: JPMorgan Chase Q2 2025 Earnings Call Transcript

sections.prepared_remarks: JPMorgan Q2 net income of $18.2 billion, up 26 percent, including a $3 billion legal reserve release. Revenue $50.3 billion, up 10 percent. Excluding the one-time benefit, adjusted net income was $15.2 billion, EPS $5.21. We returned $5.1 billion to shareholders. The legal reserve release benefited capital markets and investment banking substantially. Investment banking fees surged 43 percent year over year — we are back to 2019-2021 transaction volumes. Equity underwriting hit a record on strong IPO pipeline. FICC Markets revenue was up 19 percent in what we call a healthy volatility environment. Consumer credit actually improved slightly — card NCO rates stabilized and delinquency rates plateaued. We are seeing early signs of retail spending resilience even as higher-income consumers show caution. We continue to invest in our digital capabilities — our mobile banking app has a 4.8-star rating with 58 million users. We have deployed over 400 AI use cases internally. Our COIN platform reviews commercial credit agreements and is saving 360,000 hours of lawyer time annually.
sections.financial_highlights: Revenue $50.3 billion, EPS $6.12 reported, $5.21 adjusted. Efficiency ratio 53 percent. CET1 ratio 15.2 percent. Net interest income of $22.7 billion, down 3 percent as rate environment normalizes. Non-interest income $27.6 billion, record driven by Markets and IB strength. Deposit base remains strong at $2.6 trillion, with average consumer deposits up 3 percent. Loan growth modest at 2 percent, C&I stable, CRE moderately declining. We expect full-year 2025 EPS above $21 on adjusted basis. Capital markets revenue guidance raised — we see full-year CIB revenues 15 to 20 percent ahead of prior year. We maintained quarterly dividend of $1.40 per share. Our Markets division is well-positioned for what we expect to be an active second half in rates and credit.
sections.qanda_session:
Glazio Schold: Jamie, we've heard concerns about commercial real office exposure. Your $91 billion CRE book — what's the current occupancy rate in your collateral and what percentage of your borrowers are actively working with you on extensions versus trying to sell?

Jamie Dimon: Glazio, our office portfolio is 95 percent occupied on average, but that masks significant geographic dispersion — office in San Francisco CBD is at 55 percent occupancy, Midtown Manhattan at 60 percent, suburban and Sunbelt markets at 80 to 85 percent. We have proactively reached out to every borrower with loans over $10 million in this book. Approximately 60 percent are in active extension discussions — most of those will be extended as they come up in the next 12 months with additional collateral pledges or equity contributions. We are not seeing panic selling, but we are seeing some distressed sales. We have reserved appropriately — our office NPL rate is 1.9 percent. For comparison, we were at 2.1 percent at peak stress in 2012. We expect CRE to be a manageable headwind, not a crisis.

Brian Kleinhenz: Jeremy, on the NII guide — you've been guiding flat for several quarters but we keep getting beat. Can you walk us through the quarterly cadence and where you see positive NII surprises versus what you guided three months ago?

Jeremy Barnum: Brian, the guidance was primarily about the direction, not the exact quarterly path. The biggest positive surprise has been deposit repricing — our interest-bearing deposits repriced more slowly than we modeled, which is a positive. Also non-interest bearing deposit balances have been stickier than expected. What we didn't fully anticipate was the velocity of Markets revenue — that was a meaningful NII positive that offset the headwinds. For back-half 2025, we expect NII to be roughly flat to slightly down versus Q2. The tailwinds are moderating and the margin compression from lower rates is becoming more apparent. We still expect steady performance but the exceptional NII quarters are likely behind us.
sections.forward_outlook: Jamie Dimon: We are navigating a complex global environment with geopolitical tensions, trade policy uncertainty, and technology disruption simultaneously. Yet this firm has proven exceptionally resilient. Our investment bank is firing on all cylinders. Our consumer bank is growing, defending, and improving simultaneously. Our AI investments are paying off in risk management, customer service, and fraud. We are particularly excited about AI-driven fraud detection — our models are now identifying fraud attempts 40 percent faster than 12 months ago. We will continue to invest in talent, technology, and our global franchise. We are building for the next 50 years, not the next 50 basis points of rate moves.
